sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy remains the sole dominant market leader with an exceptional 0.950 momentum score, while Real Estate and Utilities experience sharp short-term rank deterioration.

Market leadership is exceptionally narrow, with only 1 of 11 sectors exhibiting broad-based strength across all timeframes. Energy completely anchors the top of the board as the only sustained strong sector, followed by Technology (0.700 momentum, rank 2) and Basic Materials (rank 3). Meanwhile, mid-tier sectors like Healthcare (0.717 momentum) and Financials (0.667 momentum) are showing incremental rank improvements.

At the bottom of the spectrum, defensive yield and rate-sensitive pockets are fading rapidly. Real Estate tumbled 3 spots over the last five sessions to rank 8, joined by Utilities, which dropped to rank 10 with a market-trough momentum score of 0.067. Consumer Cyclicals also remain anchored at the very bottom (rank 11) with an anemic momentum score of 0.150.

## Strength
- Energy is the only all-green sector across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD periods, leading the market with a momentum score of 0.950.
- Energy represents the sole sustained strong sector, maintaining a top-3 rank across the 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month horizons.
- Market-wide breadth is highly constrained, with only 1 of 11 groups demonstrating positive performance across all five measured timeframes.

## Movers & Momentum
- Communication Services (0.633 momentum), Consumer Defensive (0.417 momentum), Financials (0.667 momentum), and Healthcare (0.72 momentum) all advanced 1 spot in rank over the past five sessions.
- Real Estate suffered the steepest decline over five sessions, falling 3 spots to rank 8 with a momentum score of 0.333.
- The top-tier momentum leaders are Energy (0.950), Healthcare (0.717), and Technology (0.700).
- Utilities marks the weakest momentum profile across all sectors at 0.067, having dropped 1 spot to rank 10.

## Divergences
- Healthcare holds a top-two momentum score of 0.717 despite lagging at rank 6 YTD, highlighting an emerging disconnect between current velocity and YTD positioning.
- Communication Services shows strong momentum at 0.633 yet remains depressed near the bottom of the pack at rank 9.
- Industrials holds a relatively high YTD rank of 4 despite severely deteriorating momentum of 0.300, ranking it among the bottom five momentum laggards.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and defensive shipping dominate sustained momentum, while materials and alternative energy suffer sharp five-day rank deterioration.

Market leadership remains heavily concentrated, with only 14 of 144 industry groups maintaining all-green breadth across all timeframes. Traditional energy continues to set the standard, led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.980 momentum) and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.923 momentum), closely tracked by Marine Shipping (0.959 momentum). Concurrently, Diagnostics & Research is demonstrating strong dual strength, jumping 23 spots to rank 49 with an 0.880 momentum score.

Rotation is shifting away from metals, mining, and clean energy toward selective consumer defensive pockets. Coking Coal plunged 46 spots to rank 92, alongside severe drops in Uranium (-38 spots) and Aluminum (-36 spots). Meanwhile, early buying interest is emerging in lower-momentum staples like Grocery Stores and Discount Stores, even as prior momentum leaders across precious metals and Biotechnology begin to show signs of short-term fatigue.

## Strength
- **All-Green Breadth:** Just 14 of 144 groups are positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD periods, driven by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.980 momentum), Marine Shipping (0.959 momentum), and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.923 momentum).
- **Sustained Multimonth Leaders:** Groups maintaining top-36 rankings across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons include Consumer Electronics (0.909 momentum, rank YTD 29), Financial Conglomerates (0.84 momentum), Insurance - Reinsurance (0.83 momentum), and Health Information Services.
- **Top Absolute Momentum:** Energy dominates the upper echelon, with Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing holding rank 2 YTD (0.980 momentum) and Oil & Gas E&P holding rank 11 YTD (0.889 momentum).

## Movers & Momentum
- **Rapid Short-Term Gainers:** Diagnostics & Research advanced +23 spots over 5 sessions to rank 49 (0.88 momentum), followed by Insurance - Diversified (+21 spots to rank 73, 0.69 momentum) and Internet Content & Information (+20 spots to rank 68, 0.72 momentum).
- **Steep Short-Term Decliners:** Heavy industrials and materials unraveled over the past 5 sessions, led by Coking Coal (-46 spots to rank 92), Uranium (-38 spots to rank 105), and Aluminum (-36 spots to rank 89).
- **Momentum Troughs:** Footwear & Accessories anchors the bottom of the market with a 0.047 momentum score (rank 143 YTD), alongside Solar (0.097 momentum, rank 137 YTD) and Utilities - Independent Power Producers (0.099 momentum, rank 139 YTD).

## Divergences
- **Fading High-Momentum Groups:** Despite high momentum scores, selling pressure has triggered short-term rank declines in Biotechnology (0.68 momentum, falling 24 spots in 5 sessions), Copper (0.69 momentum, -8 spots), Gold (0.68 momentum, -5 spots), and Silver (0.60 momentum, -7 spots).
- **Emerging Bottom Turnarounds:** Early-stage accumulation is pushing up ranks in low-momentum consumer retail, with Grocery Stores jumping +19 spots over 5 days (0.47 momentum) and Discount Stores gaining +16 spots (0.43 momentum).
- **Secondary Early Movers:** Luxury Goods (+7 spots, 0.35 momentum) and REIT - Residential (+7 spots, 0.47 momentum) are also showing nascent rank improvement despite weak baseline momentum profiles.
